Worked example: external validation of a Cox model

Rotterdam → GBSG breast-cancer cohorts

Source: vignettes/worked_example.Rmd
worked_example.Rmd

This vignette applies the Bayesian validation framework end-to-end. We train a prognostic survival model on the Rotterdam breast-cancer cohort and externally validate it on the GBSG cohort at a clinically meaningful 5-year horizon. Every validation quantity is reported as a posterior median with a 95 % credible interval, next to the usual frequentist estimate.

The analysis runs on the coxph-Laplace backend so it reproduces with only the survival package. The primary full-Bayes path (backend = "stan_pwexp") is a drop-in replacement for the model-fitting step; everything downstream is unchanged because it consumes only the model-agnostic psurv object.

library(survival)
library(bayesval)
YEAR <- 365.25

Data: harmonising the two cohorts

Recurrence-free survival is the Rotterdam endpoint (recurrence or death); GBSG records it directly. We harmonise the shared covariates (tumour size is categorised to match Rotterdam’s factor).

prep <- function(df, time, status) {
  size_cat <- if (is.factor(df$size)) df$size else
    cut(df$size, breaks = c(-Inf, 20, 50, Inf),
        labels = c("<=20", "20-50", ">50"))
  tibble::tibble(time = df[[time]] / YEAR, status = df[[status]],
                 age = df$age, nodes = df$nodes,
                 grade3 = as.integer(df$grade >= 3),
                 size = factor(size_cat, levels = c("<=20", "20-50", ">50")),
                 logpgr = log(df$pgr + 1), hormon = df$hormon, meno = df$meno)
}
rot <- dplyr::mutate(rotterdam,
                     rfs = as.integer(recur == 1 | death == 1),
                     rfstime = ifelse(recur == 1, rtime, dtime))
train <- prep(rot, "rfstime", "rfs")  |> tidyr::drop_na()
test  <- prep(gbsg, "rfstime", "status") |> tidyr::drop_na()
horizons <- c(2, 5); h5 <- 2L; tau <- 5

Model layer: posterior survival on the external cohort

Fit on Rotterdam, then evaluate the fitted model’s Laplace posterior on GBSG.

form <- Surv(time, status) ~ age + nodes + grade3 + size + logpgr + hormon + meno
fit  <- coxph(form, data = train, x = TRUE, y = TRUE)
ps   <- psurv_external(fit, test, time = "time", status = "status",
                       horizons = horizons, S = 500L, seed = 2026)
ps
## <psurv: coxph-laplace(external)>
##   draws S = 500, subjects n = 686, horizons H = 2
##   horizons: 2, 5
##   events: 299 (56.4% censored)

Posterior validation suite

Each metric is propagated across the posterior with the Bayesian bootstrap, so the credible interval carries both model-parameter and evaluation-sample uncertainty.

suite <- list(
  harrell = metric_harrell_c,
  uno     = function(d, w) metric_uno_c(d, w, tau = tau),
  gonen   = metric_gonen_k,
  citl    = function(d, w) metric_citl(d, w)[paste0("CITL_t", h5)],
  slope   = metric_cal_slope,
  ici     = function(d, w) metric_ici(d, w, horizon = h5, method = "auto"),
  brier   = function(d, w) metric_brier(d, w)[c(paste0("Brier_t", h5), "IBS")],
  ipa     = function(d, w) metric_ipa(d, w)[paste0("IPA_t", h5)],
  r2d     = metric_r2d)
post <- propagate_many(ps, suite, weights = "bootstrap", seed = 1)
tab  <- posterior_table(post) |>
  dplyr::mutate(metric = sub("^[^.]+\\.", "", metric))
knitr::kable(dplyr::select(tab, metric, summary), caption =
             "Posterior median [95% CrI] at 5 years (param + bootstrap)")
Posterior median [95% CrI] at 5 years (param + bootstrap)
metric summary
C_harrell 0.660 [0.625, 0.690]
C_uno 0.647 [0.610, 0.678]
K_gonen 0.626 [0.614, 0.640]
CITL_t2 -0.058 [-0.153, 0.029]
cal_slope 0.796 [0.574, 1.022]
ICI 0.078 [0.022, 0.159]
E50 0.074 [0.017, 0.154]
E90 0.144 [0.050, 0.253]
Brier_t2 0.225 [0.205, 0.250]
IBS 0.200 [0.184, 0.218]
IPA_t2 0.099 [-0.007, 0.168]
R2_D 0.163 [0.105, 0.228]

Discrimination is moderate (Harrell C ≈ 0.66, Uno C ≈ 0.65). The calibration slope < 1 and ICI ≈ 0.09 flag real external miscalibration — the model’s risks need recalibration for this cohort, a conclusion discrimination alone cannot give.

Calibration as a posterior predictive check 

ppc <- ppc_calibration(ps, horizon = h5, method = "auto", draws = 200L, seed = 3)
plot_calibration_band(ppc)

Decision-analytic layer 

pnb <- posterior_net_benefit(ps, thresholds = seq(0.1, 0.7, 0.05),
                             horizon = h5, weights = "bootstrap",
                             draws = 300L, seed = 4)
plot_net_benefit(pnb)

The model’s net-benefit band lies above both “treat all” and “treat none” across clinically relevant thresholds, so it is decision-analytically useful despite the imperfect calibration.

Headline: Bayesian vs frequentist 

lp <- colMeans(ps$eta)
dfv <- tibble::tibble(time = test$time, status = test$status)
fw <- function(est, se) c(est, est - 1.96 * se, est + 1.96 * se)
ch <- concordance(Surv(time, status) ~ lp, data = dfv)
cu <- concordance(Surv(time, status) ~ lp, data = dfv, timewt = "n/G2", ymax = tau)
cs <- coxph(Surv(time, status) ~ lp, data = dfv)
freq <- tibble::tibble(
  metric = c("C_harrell", "C_uno", "cal_slope"),
  estimate = c(1 - ch$concordance, 1 - cu$concordance, coef(cs)[[1]]),
  lower = c(fw(1 - ch$concordance, sqrt(ch$var))[2],
            fw(1 - cu$concordance, sqrt(cu$var))[2],
            fw(coef(cs)[[1]], sqrt(vcov(cs)[1, 1]))[2]),
  upper = c(fw(1 - ch$concordance, sqrt(ch$var))[3],
            fw(1 - cu$concordance, sqrt(cu$var))[3],
            fw(coef(cs)[[1]], sqrt(vcov(cs)[1, 1]))[3]))
knitr::kable(posterior_vs_frequentist(tab, freq),
             caption = "Bayesian median [95% CrI] vs frequentist estimate [95% CI]")
Bayesian median [95% CrI] vs frequentist estimate [95% CI]
metric bayesian frequentist
C_harrell 0.660 [0.625, 0.690] 0.661 [0.628, 0.693]
C_uno 0.647 [0.610, 0.678] 0.648 [0.617, 0.680]
cal_slope 0.796 [0.574, 1.022] 0.769 [0.619, 0.920]

The Bayesian posterior medians reproduce the frequentist point estimates (they use the same estimators), while the credible intervals additionally propagate model-parameter uncertainty — the coherent, probabilistic replacement for the usual bootstrap CI.

The primary full-Bayes MCMC path (backend = "stan_pwexp") and internal optimism correction are covered in the package’s other articles.
